history.period: Birth site tradition from c. 1474; present temple construction date unknown
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town Birbhum is a district, not a town - the actual town/village is Ekachakra (Birchandrapur), Mayureswar-I block, Birbhum district, West Bengal, about 20 km from Rampurhat Junction. Identity CONFIRMED: the Garbhavasa (or Sootika) Mandir is the small white temple at Ekachakra marking the exact birthplace of Nityananda Prabhu, the Gaudiya Vaishnava saint who appeared here c. 1474 AD (sources differ: 1473 vs 1474) on Magha shukla trayodashi to parents Hadai Ojha/Hadai Pandita and Padmavati. Per ISKCON Mayapur's Ekachakra Dhama account, the temple was constructed by Prasannakumara Karapharma (construction date not given - flag). The complex also includes the Janmasthan Mandir (deity of Nitai worshipped by a local Brahmin family), Hadai Pandita Bhavan (father's original house site), Nitai Kund, Padmavati Kund (behind the birthplace) and the Mala Tala pippala tree associated with Nityananda's departure and Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's later visit. CSV name Lord Krishna Temple, Ekachakra is approximate: the site is specifically the Nityananda Janmasthan (Garbhavasa) temple, not a Krishna temple per se. Note: Ekachakra's name comes from the Mahabharata legend that Krishna's wheel (eka-chakra) flew from Kurukshetra and landed here during his fight with Bhishma.

name: Lord Krishna Temple, Ekachakra (Garbhavasa - birthplace of Nityananda)
town_description: Ekachakra (also written Ekacakra; at Birchandrapur) is a village in the Mayureswar-I block of Birbhum district, West Bengal, about 20 km from Rampurhat and about 212 km from Kolkata. It is one of the holiest sites of Gaudiya Vaishnavism as the birthplace of Nityananda Prabhu, drawing throngs of pilgrims, especially on Nityananda Trayodashi and Gaura Purnima. The village also preserves associated sites: Hadai Pandita Bhavan, Nitai Kund, Padmavati Kund and Mala Tala.

travel.road: Well connected by road; about 20 km from Rampurhat, 116 km from Durgapur, 212 km from Kolkata; SBSTC/NBSTC buses to Rampurhat or Tarapith, then local transport (per Wikipedia Ekachakra).
